reply.title: Why does a sigmoid squash any number into 0 to 1?
reply.story: When building models that make yes-or-no decisions, we often need to turn any score into a probability between zero and one. If we just use a linear scale, numbers can grow infinitely large or small, which breaks our rules. We need a smooth curve that gently bends to cap large values while stretching small ones. This leads us to the logistic function, a classic sigmoid curve that maps the entire real number line into a tidy interval. By adjusting the steepness parameter, we control how sharply the transition happens around the midpoint.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid maps any input into a $0$ to $1$ range. Adjust the steepness to see how the central slope changes the transition.
reply.instructions: Adjust the steepness slider to change how fast the curve transitions from zero to one. Observe the marker and readouts update instantly.
